fig1_impulse_momentum.svg: A Gaussian force pulse F(t) (shaded) delivers impulse J = integral F dt, computed by the module's impulse(). The momentum p(t)=p0+J rises by exactly the shaded area and levels off once the force ends: the impulse-momentum theorem J = Delta p.
fig2_momentum_conservation.svg: Two bodies exchange equal and opposite internal forces. Each momentum changes by its own impulse (p1 rises, p2 falls), but the total P = p1 + p2 from total_momentum() stays flat -- internal forces cannot change the total momentum.
